description: Labeled cases for tr_style_check.py — the kit's Turkish register lint. Two kinds of rule live in it and the set covers both: settled orthography (percent placement, vb./vs.) where one form is simply wrong, and contested convention (decimal separator, voice) where the checker must flag the MIXTURE and never the choice. Most cases pin `checks` to one detector so a case measures the rule it names; the last two run the full set to prove the detectors do not cross-fire. Negatives outnumber positives and are near-misses by construction: the section number that looks like a decimal, the first-mention English parenthetical, the noun that ends in -tık.

cases.comment: NEGATIVE, and load-bearing. 'artık' is a noun (residual), not a -dık verb. The counts are deliberate: eight impersonal predicates clear VOICE_MIN_TOTAL on their own, so the case cannot pass by falling under the floor, and three 'artık' occurrences would put the first-person share at 0.27 — above VOICE_MIX_FLOOR — the moment FIRST_PERSON_EXCEPTIONS stops working. Residual analysis is where a real Turkish methods section says the word this often.

cases.comment: NEGATIVE, and it exists for a reason worth stating: adding case 114 (a true positive) raised this set's tp from 8 to 9, which lifted the precision the mutation 'first-person-exception-list-emptied' produces from 8/9 = 0.89 to 9/10 = 0.90 — exactly the threshold — and the mutation started SURVIVING. Mutation catching is threshold-based, so a set can lose a mutation by gaining a positive. The fix is a second negative that also dies under it: with two false positives the mutated checker scores 9/11 = 0.82 and is caught again. Same arithmetic as 107 (eight impersonal predicates clear VOICE_MIN_TOTAL, three 'atık' tokens clear VOICE_MIX_FLOOR), different exception word, so the two cases cannot both be satisfied by special-casing one noun.

mutations.breaks: '25%' stops being reported, so the one settled orthography rule in the checker silently stops applying.
'v.b.' stops being distinguished from the correct 'vb.'.
'Bolum 3.1' and 'Tablo 2.4' start counting as decimal points, so a manuscript that holds the comma convention is reported as mixing separators.
Nouns ending in -tik/-dik ('artik' = residual) start reading as first-person verbs, so an impersonal manuscript is reported as mixing voice.
The single English parenthetical at first mention stops being exempt, so correct academic practice is reported as a term-unity defect.
Any trace of the minority register counts as mixing, so a manuscript that holds one voice with a single exception is flagged.
A figure reported in the Ozet but not the Abstract stops being detected - the single most common defect the check exists for.

A DOI's registrant prefix (10.17780) goes back to being counted as a decimal point, so a review citing many DOIs has them stuffed onto the dot side of the very tally that decides which convention dominates — and can be told its comma-consistent manuscript is mixed.

The English Abstract goes back to being linted as Turkish prose, so its correct '94.2%' and '0.942' are reported as orthography errors and are counted on the minority side of the tally that decides which convention the Turkish body uses. The same line now also carries the generated-file exemption, so removing it re-admits machine-emitted tables quoting English source strings.
A hard-wrapped keyword list is truncated at its first newline, so two lists holding the same terms are reported as different lengths, and a genuine mismatch hiding past the wrap goes unseen.

Every quoted product version ('IDx-DR 2.0', 'RetCAD v.2.2.0') goes back to counting as a decimal point, so a manuscript whose own numbers are uniformly comma-written is reported as mixing separators — and cannot fix it without misquoting its sources.
